concept.name: Death cross
concept.definition: A bearish moving-average crossover — classically the 50-day SMA crossing below the 200-day SMA — read as confirmation of a long-term downtrend; the mirror image of the golden cross and equally a convention rather than a proven law.
concept.intuition: The medium-term average sinking below the long-term average suggests the decline has been deep and persistent enough to bend long-term trend measures.
concept.mechanics: The shorter (typically 50-day) moving average crosses down through the longer (typically 200-day) one; like the golden cross, it lags and typically prints well after the actual top.
concept.failure_modes: Late and whipsaw-prone in sideways markets; many historical death crosses have occurred near market lows rather than before extended declines.
concept.misconceptions: A death cross does not forecast a crash — it records that a decline has already been large enough to pull the 50-day average below the 200-day.
concept.example: MACD(50,200,1) turning negative marks the same 50/200 EMA death cross in oscillator form.

citations.source: Moving Averages - Simple and Exponential | ChartSchool | StockCharts.com
